newsitem.title: USA: WMX says Soros group too late with its board nominees.
newsitem.headline: WMX says Soros group too late with its board nominees.

text.p: WMX Technologies Inc. said Wednesday that a slate of directors proposed by investors led by financier George Soros does not qualify for consideration at the company's annual meeting this year.

"The documents we received from the Soros group attempting to nominate four individuals for election as directors of the company arrived after the filing deadline and contained incomplete information," WMX said in a statement.
WMX added, however, that its board was committed to search for the best possible candidates and its nominating committee had agreed to consider the Soros nominees later this year.
"Our board is absolutely committed to attracting the best directors possible. We want to make sure we are serving the interests of all of our stockholders," WMX said.
WMX, based in Oak Brook, Ill., announced last week that it was cutting 3,000 jobs and shedding $1.5 billion in assets in a broad restructuring as it refocuses on the waste management business.

On Tuesday the Soros group expressed dissatisfaction with the restructuring plan and proposed removing WMX President and Chief Executive Phillip Rooney as well as nominating four candidates to be WMX directors.
WMX, which last week reported a fourth-quarter loss of $461 million, also said Wednesday that its board unanimously reaffirmed its support for Rooney and his leadership.
It said that Rooney, a long-time manager of the company's waste management business, was the right leader for the company as it concentrates on that industry.

WMX also said an important component of its restructuring plan was adding new, independent perspectives to its board and said it had engaged the services of an executive recruiting firm to find appropriate candidates.
WMX stock, which fell 9 percent after last week's announcements, added 12.5 cents to $32.125 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
